html:
The Angaité are an Indigenous people of the Paraguayan Chaco, west of the Paraguay River in Paraguay. Their language belongs to the Enlhet-Enenlhet family, with those of the Enxet, Sanapaná and Toba-Enenlhet.

In the late 1800s much of their land was sold to companies cutting quebracho trees for tannin, and many Angaité worked for them. The Chaco War of 1932 to 1935 was fought across the region. Many Angaité children now speak only Guarani.
